title: Ricci flow for the Bures--Helstrom qubit metric
abstract: The Bures--Helstrom metric is the minimal monotone Riemannian metric on the state space of a qubit. With the quantum Fisher normalization used here, it identifies the Bloch ball with a geodesic hemisphere of the unit round three--sphere. We describe its Ricci flow explicitly. In a general rotationally symmetric gauge the flow is a coupled system for the radial lapse and warping factor; a single scalar equation appears only after a Hamilton--DeTurck gauge choice. In the corresponding moving DeTurck frame the squared warping function $Ψ=Φ^2$ satisfies the linear forced heat equation \begin{equation*} D_tΨ=Ψ_{ss}-2, \end{equation*} while the fixed-lapse coordinate form contains the associated transport term. Since the Bures--Helstrom metric is Einstein, the geometric flow itself is the homothetic shrinker \begin{equation*} g(t)=(1-4t)g_{\mathrm{BH}}, \end{equation*} with scalar curvature $6/(1-4t)$ and extinction time $T=1/4$. Thus the metric remains inside the monotone cone for all $t<T$ and leaves the cone of nondegenerate Riemannian metrics only through the collapsed limit. We also record the volume--normalized flow, for which the Bures--Helstrom metric is a fixed point. Its linearization is the shifted round--sphere Laplacian $Δ_{\mathbb S^3}+3$, with spectrum \begin{equation*} σ_\ell=-(\ell-1)(\ell+3), \end{equation*} and spectral gap $5$ after removal of the scaling mode.
summary: This paper applies Ricci flow theory to analyze the geometry of the qubit state space, specifically using the Bures--Helstrom metric. It shows that while the unnormalized flow collapses in finite time, the volume-normalized flow stabilizes at the Bures--Helstrom metric, confirming its role as a geometrically stable fixed point within the cone of monotone metrics.
main_problem: The paper describes the intrinsic Ricci flow of the Bures--Helstrom metric on the state space of a qubit.
main_result: The unnormalized flow exhibits finite-time collapse as a homothetic shrinker, while the volume-normalized flow fixes this scale and shows the Bures--Helstrom metric is an asymptotically stable fixed point.
method: The analysis employs Ricci flow techniques, utilizing gauge fixing (Hamilton--DeTurck) to reduce the evolution equations for the warping factor ($\Phi$) to a linear forced heat equation in specific coordinates.
model_or_system: The system is the state space of a single qubit, whose geometry is endowed with the Bures--Helstrom metric. This metric is characterized as the minimal monotone Riemannian metric on this space.
key_observables: Warping function ($\Phi$) and its square ($\Psi$), scalar curvature ($R$), and the flow's evolution relative to the homothetic shrinker $g(t)=(1-4t)g_{\mathrm{BH}}$.
important_parameters: The extinction time for the unnormalized flow is $T=1/4$. The spectral gap of the linearized normalized flow is 5.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes rotational symmetry for the metric and relies on choosing specific gauges, such as the Hamilton--DeTurck gauge, to simplify the differential equations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the contraction of the warping profile ($\Phi$) and the divergence of scalar curvature ($R/6 \propto 1/(1-4t)$) at $T=1/4$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Bures--Helstrom metric as an Einstein manifold. It then derives the coupled Ricci flow equations for general rotationally symmetric metrics, fixes the gauge to obtain a single scalar equation for $\Psi$, and finally analyzes both the unnormalized (collapsing) and volume-normalized (stable fixed point) flows.
why_interesting: The application of geometric evolution equations like Ricci flow to quantum state spaces provides deep insights into how physical constraints (like monotonicity) dictate the long-term dynamics of quantum information measures. The explicit solvability of this specific metric is a major theoretical achievement.
